title: Common Errors
markdown:
Most bugs in this course are not compiler errors: the program runs, but gives a wrong answer, crashes on some inputs, or is far too slow. Test small cases by hand, the edge cases (empty input, one element, all equal, sorted, reversed) and large inputs.

## Wrong answers

| Symptom | Usual cause | Fix | Lesson |
|---|---|---|---|
| Binary search loops forever or misses the first/last element | Inconsistent range convention, or `lo = mid` with `mid` rounded down | Use a half-open `[lo, hi)` range and an invariant; when setting `lo = mid`, round `mid` up | 2.01 |
| Wrong result for large values | `(lo + hi) / 2` or a sum overflowing `int` | `lo + (hi - lo) / 2`; accumulate in `long long` | 2.01 |
| A sort crashes or returns garbage | A comparator using `<=` (not a strict weak ordering) | Compare with `<`, and `std::tie` for several keys | 3.01 |
| Equal elements change order after sorting | `std::sort` is not stable | `std::stable_sort` | 3.01 |
| BFS gives wrong distances or is slow | Marking vertices visited when popped, so they are queued many times | Mark (set the distance) when pushing | 5.01 |
| Dijkstra gives a wrong distance | A negative edge weight | Bellman-Ford, or reformulate without negative weights | 5.03 |
| Dijkstra stops too early for a target | Returning when the target is pushed, not popped | Stop when it is popped | 5.03 |
| A directed graph is reported cyclic when it is not | Treating an edge to any visited vertex as a cycle | Only an edge to a grey (in-progress) vertex is a cycle | 5.02 |
| A hash set misses keys that are present | The hash disagrees with `==` (equal keys hash differently) | Hash exactly the fields `==` compares | 2.02 |
| Linear probing loses keys after erase | Erasing by emptying the slot | Use tombstones or backward-shift deletion | 2.04 |
| 0/1 knapsack uses an item twice | One-row DP looping capacities upwards | Loop capacities from high to low | 6.03 |
| "Ways to make change" counts 1+3 and 3+1 separately | Amounts in the outer loop | Coins in the outer loop for combinations | 6.02 |
| Greedy gives a non-optimal answer | No greedy-choice property (coins 1, 3, 4; 0/1 knapsack) | Look for a counterexample; use DP | 6.01 |
| Union-find answers are wrong | Uniting `a` and `b` instead of their roots | `parent[find(b)] = find(a)` | 4.05 |
| AVL tree heights or sizes are wrong after rotations | Updating the new root before the old one | Update the lower node first, then the node that moved up | 4.03 |

## Crashes and undefined behaviour

| Symptom | Usual cause | Fix | Lesson |
|---|---|---|---|
| Crash after `push_back` | A pointer, reference or iterator into a vector that reallocated | Keep indexes, or `reserve` first | 1.03 |
| Stack overflow on large inputs | Deep recursion: DFS on a long path, destroying a long linked list, quicksort on sorted input | Iterate with an explicit stack; destroy lists in a loop; recurse on the smaller side | 1.04, 3.03, 5.02 |
| Crash on an empty container | `front()`, `back()`, `top()` or `pop()` on an empty container | Check `empty()` first | 1.05 |
| Index out of range in a segment tree | An array of `2n` for the recursive version | Allocate `4n` for the recursive layout | 4.04 |
| Reading freed memory in a linked list | Using a node after `unique_ptr` released it | Read what you need (key, next) before moving the pointer | 1.04 |
| `vector<bool>` surprises | It is a packed bitset, not a real `vector` of `bool` | Use `std::vector<char>` when you need references or speed per element | 4.05 |

## Too slow

| Symptom | Usual cause | Fix | Lesson |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fine for 1,000 items, hopeless for 100,000 | An O(n²) algorithm hidden in a loop: `find`, `erase(begin())`, `insert` at the front, copying a vector per call | Choose an O(n log n) or O(n) method; pass by reference | 1.01 |
| A hash table is slow | Many collisions from a poor hash (summing characters, XOR of fields, multiples of the bucket count) | Use a mixing hash; combine fields with a mixing formula | 2.02 |
| Plain BST becomes slow | Keys inserted in sorted order make a list | Use a balanced tree (AVL, `std::map`) | 4.02 |
| Recursion recomputes the same values | No memoisation | Cache results, or tabulate | 6.02 |
| Backtracking never finishes | Pruning too late or not at all | Check constraints as soon as a choice is made; choose the most constrained variable first | 6.05 |
| Debug build far slower than expected | Debug iterators and no optimisation | Measure in a Release build | 1.02 |
